Everything You Need to Know About CNC Lathing Published Nov 30, 2025, updated Nov 29, 2025 11 min Table of Contents Understanding CNC Lathes How CNC Lathe Machines Work Common Types of CNC Lathe Machines CNC Lathe vs Other CNC Machines How Much Does a CNC Lathe Cost? Applications of CNC Lathes FAQ (AI-generated) CNC lathes remain one of the most important machine types in modern manufacturing, powering industries from automotive to aerospace with accuracy, speed, and repeatability. If you're researching CNC lathing for your next project—or comparing CNC lathe machines, CNC machine lathes, or even trying to understand what is a CNC lathe —this guide gives you everything you need to make informed decisions. And if you're looking for fast, reliable machining services, JLCCNC provides high-precision CNC turning and milling with instant quoting and a wide selection of materials to support both prototyping and production. Understanding CNC Lathes Definition and Key Components of a CNC Lathe A CNC lathe is a computer-controlled machine tool designed to rotate a workpiece while cutting tools remove material to create cylindrical or conical geometries. Unlike manual lathes, CNC lathe machines operate through programmed commands, ensuring consistent dimensions even across large production batches. A typical CNC lathe machine includes: Headstock : houses the spindle that rotates the part Chuck : grips the material Tool turret : holds multiple CNC tools Bed & carriage : provide machine rigidity Control system : executes CNC turning programs Tailstock (optional): supports long workpieces These elements work together to deliver smooth, accurate cutting, making CNC lathing suitable for both simple shafts and highly complex components. Differences Between CNC Lathes and Conventional Lathes Conventional lathes require manual adjustments, which slows down production and introduces human error. A CNC machine lathe, by contrast, runs automated toolpaths defined in G-code. The benefits include: Faster cycle times Higher precision and repeatability Better safety Ability to handle complex geometries Automated multi-tool operations For manufacturers needing accuracy within microns or consistent production day after day, CNC lathes outperform manual machines in every category. Core Advantages of CNC Lathing CNC lathing offers several strong advantages: Superior roundness and concentricity for rotational parts Excellent surface finish due to continuous cutting Strong material compatibility , including aluminum, steel, stainless steel, copper, brass, plastics, and more Great scalability , from prototypes to mass production Tight tolerances , often ±0.005 mm on high-end systems These strengths explain why CNC lathe machines remain foundational in nearly all manufacturing sectors. How CNC Lathe Machines Work (AI-generated) Overview of the Lathing Process The CNC lathing process begins by mounting raw material—typically a bar or billet—into the chuck. As the spindle rotates the workpiece, CNC cutting tools move linearly along X and Z axes to remove material and create the desired geometry. CNC lathing is especially efficient for: Shafts Pins Bushings Sleeves Threads Custom cylindrical forms Because the workpiece rotates while the tool moves, the process is optimized for parts where diameter features dominate. CNC Programming Basics for Turning Operations At the heart of every CNC lathe machine is a program composed of G-code and M-code . These commands tell the machine: How fast to the spindle rotate How quickly do cutting tools feed into the material Which tools to activate What path should the tool follow Programs are often written manually for simple parts or generated with CAD/CAM software for complex geometries. Understanding these fundamentals is essential for efficient CNC lathing. Motion Control and Spindle Operation CNC lathes synchronize motion between the spindle and cutting tools. Toolpaths rely on precise feed rates, calculated surface speeds, and appropriate depth of cut. Advanced CNC machine lathes use: Servo motors for precise tool motion Variable-frequency drives to control spindle speed Automatic tool changers for seamless multi-operation machining Together, these systems deliver both speed and accuracy. Common Types of CNC Lathe Machines Horizontal CNC Lathes Horizontal CNC lathes are the most widely used type of turning equipment, with the spindle oriented parallel to the machine bed. They excel at machining long, cylindrical parts and support both small-batch and mass production. Because chips naturally fall away from the cutting zone, these machines offer excellent chip evacuation, stable cutting conditions, and flexible turret configurations. Sizes range from compact turning centers—ideal for small parts—to heavy-duty industrial lathes capable of handling workpieces hundreds of millimeters in diameter. Many horizontal machines can be equipped with bar feeders, automatic loading systems, and sub-spindles to improve throughput. Key factors to evaluate include bed rigidity, spindle torque and speed, turret capacity, and the maximum turning diameter/length ratio (L/D), which influences stability and machining efficiency. Typical applications: shafts, bearing housings, cylinders, gear blanks, and various rotational components. Vertical CNC Lathes Vertical CNC lathes position the spindle vertically, with the workpiece mounted on a horizontal table. This configuration is ideal for large-diameter, short-height components, as gravity assists with part positioning and workholding stability. It also makes loading heavy parts safer and easier. Vertical lathes are known for exceptional rigidity when handling large, heavy, or wide workpieces, making them a staple in industries requiring oversized components. Important considerations include maximum turning diameter, table load capacity, machine rigidity, and spindle power. Typical applications: large flanges, disks, turbine housings, rotors, and components for wind power, construction, and heavy machinery. Precision CNC Lathes and Multi-Axis Machines Precision CNC lathes and multi-axis turning centers are designed for complex geometries and ultra-tight tolerances. These machines often include high-precision linear guides, thermal compensation systems, scale feedback, and advanced CNC controls. Multi-axis machines may integrate C-axis, Y-axis, sub-spindles, and driven tooling, allowing complete machining—turning, milling, drilling, and tapping—in a single setup. This reduces cycle time, improves accuracy, and eliminates secondary operations. Precision machines commonly use high-speed, low-vibration spindles and rigid tooling systems (such as HSK or BT holders) to deliver micron-level accuracy and excellent surface finishes. Typical applications: medical implants, aerospace components, precision instrument parts, high-end mold components, and any part requiring complex profiles or tight tolerances. CNC Lathe vs Other CNC Machines Key differences between CNC lathes and mills A CNC lathe operates by rotating the workpiece at high speed while the cutting tool remains stationary or moves along a controlled axis. This turning-based process makes it exceptionally effective for producing round, tubular, and symmetrical shapes with consistent concentricity. CNC mills, on the other hand, remove material using a rotating cutting tool that moves across multiple axes. Milling machines are better suited for flat surfaces, slots, pockets, and complex 3D forms. Compared with milling, a CNC lathe generally delivers higher efficiency for rotational components, faster material removal for cylindrical profiles, and tighter geometric tolerances for features such as diameters, tapers, and threads. If you're interested in understanding milling processes in more depth, you can continue with our Bed Milling Explained . Advantages of using a lathe for specific parts When manufacturing shafts, bushings, pins, spacers, and threaded connectors, a CNC lathe offers superior stability and repeatability. The continuous rotation of the workpiece allows for smooth surface finishes and accurate dimensional control, especially on long or slender parts. For high-volume production, the turning process significantly reduces cycle time, lowering overall machining costs. Modern CNC lathes can also integrate operations such as drilling, tapping, grooving, and parting directly into the same setup, minimizing repositioning errors. This combined functionality is highly beneficial for parts that require multiple machining steps but must maintain tight tolerance alignment across all features. Application scenarios A CNC lathe is widely applied across automotive, aerospace, medical devices, consumer electronics, industrial automation, and custom hardware manufacturing. Common examples include motor shafts, gear blanks, threaded inserts, precision fasteners, hydraulic fittings, valve components, connector housings, bearing parts, and high-accuracy prototypes. It is especially valuable in scenarios where roundness, diameter precision, and concentricity are critical. In prototyping, a CNC lathe supports quick iteration with consistent dimensional results, while in mass production, it ensures stable quality with efficient material utilization and reduced machining time. How Much Does a CNC Lathe Cost? Factors Affecting CNC Lathe Pricing CNC lathe machine cost varies widely. Key pricing factors include: Machine size and rigidity Horizontal vs vertical configuration Precision and number of axes Control system brand Maximum spindle speed Tool turret capacity Production-grade CNC lathes typically cost more because they offer tighter tolerances and faster cycle times. Typical Cost Ranges Approximate global pricing: Entry-level CNC lathes : $6,000–$15,000 Mid-range industrial machines : $20,000–$80,000 High-end multi-axis lathes : $100,000–$350,000+ Operational costs—tooling, maintenance, power—should also be considered. Tips to Optimize Machining Cost Choose the right machine size for your parts Avoid unnecessary tolerances Select easily machinable materials Minimize tool changes Optimize programming to reduce air-cutting time For outsourcing, JLCCNC offers instant quoting that automatically identifies cost-drivers, helping teams refine designs early. High efficiency and speed Automated turning dramatically shortens cycle times for cylindrical components compared with manual lathes or milling solutions. Superior surface finishes Lathes can achieve extremely smooth finishes—often without secondary grinding—reducing total manufacturing time. Wide material compatibility Metals (aluminum, steel, stainless steel, brass, copper, titanium), plastics, and composites can all be effectively machined. Whether for precision machining, high-volume production, or rapid prototyping, CNC lathes remain one of the most versatile and indispensable tools in modern manufacturing. FAQ Q1: What is a CNC lathe used for? A CNC lathe is used to machine round or cylindrical parts with high precision, such as shafts, bushings, and threaded components. Q2: Is CNC lathing different from CNC turning? No. CNC lathing and CNC turning refer to the same subtractive manufacturing process. Q3: What materials can be machined on a CNC lathe machine? Common materials include aluminum, steel, stainless steel, copper alloys, brass, titanium, plastics, and composites. Q4: Do CNC lathes support automation? Yes. Many CNC lathe machines integrate automatic bar feeders, robotic loading, and tool monitoring for continuous production. Q5: What is the difference between CNC lathes and CNC mills? Lathes rotate the workpiece; mills rotate the tool. Lathes are ideal for round parts; mills are ideal for prismatic shapes. Application scenarios A CNC lathe is widely applied across automotive, aerospace, medical devices, consumer electronics, industrial automation, and custom hardware manufacturing. Common examples include motor shafts, gear blanks, threaded inserts, precision fasteners, hydraulic fittings, valve components, connector housings, bearing parts, and high-accuracy prototypes. It is especially valuable in scenarios where roundness, diameter precision, and concentricity are critical. In prototyping, a CNC lathe supports quick iteration with consistent dimensional results, while in mass production, it ensures stable quality with efficient material utilization and reduced machining time. How Much Does a CNC Lathe Cost? Factors Affecting CNC Lathe Pricing CNC lathe machine cost varies widely. Key pricing factors include: Machine size and rigidity Horizontal vs vertical configuration Precision and number of axes Control system brand Maximum spindle speed Tool turret capacity Production-grade CNC lathes typically cost more because they offer tighter tolerances and faster cycle times. Typical Cost Ranges Approximate global pricing: Entry-level CNC lathes : $6,000–$15,000 Mid-range industrial machines : $20,000–$80,000 High-end multi-axis lathes : $100,000–$350,000+ Operational costs—tooling, maintenance, power—should also be considered. Applications of CNC Lathes (AI-generated) CNC lathes play a foundational role in modern manufacturing because they can produce rotational, symmetric, and highly accurate parts at scale. Their precision, repeatability, and ability to cut complex geometries with minimal human intervention make them essential across countless industries. Whether the requirement is tight tolerances, smooth surface finishes, or efficient mass production, CNC lathing remains one of the most reliable machining processes in use today. Industries Using CNC Lathes CNC lathes are used in nearly every engineering sector, but several industries rely on them heavily due to the demanding tolerances and durability their components require: Automotive & Transportation Engine components, shafts, bushings, fasteners, gearbox parts, and custom aftermarket components are frequently produced by CNC lathes. High-volume turning ensures consistent performance under thermal and mechanical stress. Aerospace & Defense Precision is non-negotiable in aerospace. CNC lathes produce lightweight, high-strength components such as actuator housings, turbine rings, hydraulic fittings, and threaded connectors with strict tolerance control. Industrial Machinery & Robotics CNC lathes create spindle components, couplings, rollers, sleeves, and automation parts that require stable roundness and wear resistance for long-term performance. Electronics & Energy Connectors, insulators, sensor housings, and precision terminals are often lathe-machined. In the energy sector, CNC lathes support oil & gas tools, power equipment, and high-pressure fittings. Medical Devices Surgical instruments, orthopedic implants, dental components, and small precision parts benefit from the lathe's ability to deliver micron-level accuracy and clean surface finishes. Custom Manufacturing & Prototyping For low-volume custom parts, CNC lathes provide fast turnaround, tight tolerances, and cost-effective production—ideal for R&D teams and product development. Common Parts Produced by CNC Lathes Because lathes specialize in rotational parts, the most frequently produced components include: Shafts, rods, axles, and pins Sleeves, bushings, spacers Nuts, bolts, threaded inserts Fittings and couplings Housings and cylindrical enclosures Hydraulic and pneumatic components Bearings rings and precision rollers These parts typically require excellent concentricity, smooth surface finish, and predictable dimensional accuracy—strengths that CNC lathes consistently deliver. Benefits in Manufacturing The widespread use of CNC lathes stems from several tangible advantages that make them valuable in both prototype and production environments: Outstanding repeatability Once programmed, CNC lathes replicate parts with minimal deviation, making them ideal for mass production. High efficiency and speed Automated turning dramatically shortens cycle times for cylindrical components compared with manual lathes or milling solutions. Superior surface finishes Lathes can achieve extremely smooth finishes—often without secondary grinding—reducing total manufacturing time. Wide material compatibility Metals (aluminum, steel, stainless steel, brass, copper, titanium), plastics, and composites can all be effectively machined. Cost-effective production For cylindrical parts, CNC lathing is often the most economical manufacturing method due to optimized toolpaths and reduced machining passes. Whether for precision machining, high-volume production, or rapid prototyping, CNC lathes remain one of the most versatile and indispensable tools in modern manufacturing. FAQ Q1: What is a CNC lathe used for? A CNC lathe is used to machine round or cylindrical parts with high precision, such as shafts, bushings, and threaded components. Q2: Is CNC lathing different from CNC turning? No. CNC lathing and CNC turning refer to the same subtractive manufacturing process. Q3: What materials can be machined on a CNC lathe machine? Common materials include aluminum, steel, stainless steel, copper alloys, brass, titanium, plastics, and composites. Q4: Do CNC lathes support automation? Yes. Many CNC lathe machines integrate automatic bar feeders, robotic loading, and tool monitoring for continuous production. Q5: What is the difference between CNC lathes and CNC mills? Lathes rotate the workpiece; mills rotate the tool. Lathes are ideal for round parts; mills are ideal for prismatic shapes. Rather than focusing on individual machines, CNC technology connects digital design, machining processes, and quality systems into an integrated manufacturing workflow. This allows manufacturers to achieve higher throughput, tighter tolerances, and more predictable production outcomes across the entire product lifecycle. By integrating digital design files with computer-controlled machinery, CNC systems allow manufacturers to produce complex parts with consistent accuracy, scalability, and efficiency. From prototyping to full-scale industrial production, CNC technology supports faster workflows, tighter tolerances, and seamless coordination between design, machining, and quality control. For readers who want a clear definition of CNC and a foundational explanation of how CNC machines operate, we provide a dedicated CNC meaning and definition guide that focuses specifically on terminology and basic concepts. To translate CNC technology into real manufacturing outcomes, professional machining services play a critical role. JLCCNC provides CNC machining solutions that support prototyping, small-batch production, and industrial-scale manufacturing, enabling companies to apply CNC technology efficiently without investing in in-house capacity. What is CNC Technology? CNC technology refers to the integrated use of software, control systems, and automated machinery to manage and execute precision manufacturing processes. In modern production environments, CNC technology functions as a core manufacturing platform—linking digital design data with machining operations, tool management, and quality control systems. Advantages of CNC Technology CNC technology offers a wide range of advantages that make it essential to modern manufacturing. By combining computer-controlled automation with high-performance machinery, CNC systems significantly improve manufacturing efficiency. They also enable superior quality and scalability across diverse industries. High Precision and Consistent Accuracy One of the most significant advantages of CNC technology is its ability to deliver extremely high precision. CNC technology can repeatedly produce components with tight tolerances that are difficult or impossible to achieve through manual machining. Once a program is validated, the same dimensions and surface quality can be maintained across thousands of parts, ensuring consistent accuracy even in complex geometries. This level of precision is especially critical in industries such as aerospace, automotive, medical devices, and electronics, where small dimensional deviations can affect performance, safety, or compliance with industry standards. Increased Production Efficiency CNC technology dramatically improves production efficiency by automating machining operations. Machines can run continuously with minimal operator intervention, reducing setup time and accelerating production cycles. Multi-axis CNC systems further enhance efficiency by completing multiple operations—such as milling, drilling, and contouring—in a single setup. Automated tool changes, optimized tool paths, and high-speed machining capabilities allow manufacturers to shorten lead times and respond quickly to changing production demands. Excellent Repeatability and Quality Control Repeatability is a core strength of CNC technology. Every part produced from the same CNC program is virtually identical, minimizing variation and reducing scrap rates. This repeatability simplifies quality control processes, as fewer manual inspections are required once a process is stabilized. CNC systems also integrate easily with in-process measurement and inspection technologies, enabling real-time quality monitoring and early detection of deviations before defects occur. Material and Design Versatility CNC technology supports a wide range of materials, including metals, plastics, composites, and engineered alloys. From aluminum and stainless steel to advanced polymers and titanium, CNC machines can be optimized to handle different cutting characteristics and surface finish requirements. A common example is aluminum CNC machining , which is widely used due to aluminum’s excellent machinability and strength-to-weight ratio. In addition, CNC technology enables the machining of complex shapes, internal features, and intricate contours that would be extremely time-consuming or impractical with conventional methods. This design freedom allows engineers to innovate without being limited by manufacturing constraints. Scalability from Prototyping to Mass Production Another key advantage of CNC technology is its scalability. The same CNC setup can be used for rapid prototyping, small-batch production, and high-volume manufacturing with minimal modification. Design changes can be implemented quickly by updating the digital program rather than retooling entire production lines. This flexibility is particularly valuable for startups, R&D teams, and manufacturers operating in fast-moving markets where product iterations are frequent. Reduced Labor Dependency and Improved Safety By automating machining tasks, CNC technology reduces reliance on manual labor and lowers the risk of human error. Operators are less exposed to cutting tools and moving machine components, resulting in a safer working environment. Modern CNC systems also feature built-in safety controls, error detection, and machine monitoring functions that further protect both personnel and equipment while maintaining stable production. Cost Efficiency Over the Product Lifecycle While CNC machines require an initial investment, they offer long-term cost advantages. Reduced material waste, lower rework rates, shorter production times, and improved machine utilization all contribute to a lower cost per part over the product lifecycle. For manufacturers seeking consistent quality, predictable output, and efficient resource usage, CNC technology represents a cost-effective solution that supports sustainable growth. Applications of CNC Technology in Manufacturing CNC technology has a wide range of applications across industries due to its ability to deliver high precision, consistency, and production efficiency. From large-scale industrial manufacturing to rapid prototyping, CNC technology continues to expand as materials, software, and machine capabilities evolve. Applications in Metalworking CNC milling machines, lathes, and laser cutters handle metals like aluminum, steel, and titanium with unmatched precision. These machines reduce manual labor, minimize errors, and allow for complex shapes that meet rigorous industry standards. In metalworking industries where tolerance control and material consistency are critical, CNC technology enables reliable production of complex metal components at scale. Applications in Plastics and Woodworking Beyond metals, CNC routers can cut, engrave, and shape plastic components or wood panels with high accuracy. Routers are typically used for wood and plastic materials, while milling machines are better suited for metal machining due to their rigidity and cutting capabilities. Manufacturers can efficiently produce prototypes and mass-produced items, lowering production costs and turnaround times. Industrial Applications Industries such as automotive, aerospace, electronics, energy, and heavy machinery rely on CNC systems to produce structural components, housings, brackets, and precision parts. CNC machining ensures tight tolerances, repeatability, and high reliability for critical components. Prototyping and Small Batch Production Rapid prototyping and small-batch CNC production allow engineers to quickly transform digital designs into functional prototypes, enabling faster design validation, iterative testing, and reduced time-to-market. Innovative Uses in Various Industries Advanced applications such as multi-axis cutting, hybrid additive-subtractive manufacturing, and complex 3D contour machining expand possibilities in medical devices, architecture, and custom design. CNC Machine Technology Types of CNC Machines CNC machine technology includes milling machines, lathes, routers, plasma cutters, and laser engraving systems. Each type serves a specific function, from cutting and drilling to shaping and engraving, meeting diverse manufacturing needs. How CNC Machines Work CNC machines operate by translating digital designs into precise machining actions through integrated control systems. This enables highly accurate and repeatable production while minimizing material waste and optimizing workflow efficiency. Maintenance and Optimization Proper maintenance of CNC machines is essential for long-term performance. Regular calibration, tool replacement, and software updates optimize machine efficiency and prevent downtime. Skilled operators can further enhance productivity by choosing the right tooling and machining parameters. Industrial CNC Technology Automation in Large-Scale Production Industrial CNC technology enables full automation of production lines. Large-scale manufacturing can run continuously with minimal human supervision, improving throughput and reducing labor costs. Integration with Industrial Processes CNC technology integrates seamlessly with industrial processes such as assembly, quality inspection, and material handling. This integration allows for smarter factories, streamlined workflows, and higher overall efficiency. Case Studies Industries adopting industrial CNC technology have reported reduced production errors, faster turnaround times, and improved product consistency. For example, automotive suppliers use CNC machines to produce engine components with precise tolerances, enhancing vehicle performance and reliability. CNC Technology Services Design and Consulting Services CNC technology services extend beyond machining itself. Design and consulting services help manufacturers apply CNC technology effectively by optimizing material selection, machining strategies, and process planning before production begins. Manufacturing and Prototyping Services Service providers offer CNC machining for both prototypes and mass production. This allows businesses to outsource specialized tasks, reduce overhead, and maintain high-quality standards. Maintenance and Support Services Many CNC technology service providers also offer ongoing maintenance, troubleshooting, and training. This ensures clients can maintain efficient operations, extend machine lifespan, and minimize production delays. Future Trends in CNC Technology Beyond basic CNC operation and machine control, future CNC technology development is increasingly driven by intelligence, connectivity, and system-level integration. Future developments will not only improve precision and productivity but also fundamentally reshape how factories operate, how products are designed, and how manufacturers compete in global markets. Smart CNC and AI Integration The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with CNC systems is transforming machining from reactive automation into predictive and adaptive manufacturing. AI-powered algorithms can analyze historical machining data. They automatically optimize tool paths, reduce cycle times, and minimize tool wear. Machine learning models are increasingly used to detect subtle signs of tool degradation or misalignment before they cause defects. In aerospace and medical device manufacturing, where tolerances are extremely tight, AI-assisted CNC tool path optimization is already being adopted to ensure consistency and precision across complex geometries. Over time, smart CNC machines will be able to adjust cutting strategies in real time, self-correcting for material inconsistencies and dynamic load variations without human intervention. IoT and Connected Manufacturing The rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) enables CNC machines to become integral components of connected smart factories. Sensors embedded in CNC equipment collect real-time data on temperature, vibration, spindle load, and tool life. This data, streamed through secure networks, feeds into centralized manufacturing execution systems (MES) and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems to support real-time monitoring and informed decision-making. Connected CNC machines can automatically schedule maintenance based on actual usage patterns, reducing unplanned downtime. In facilities with multiple machines producing different parts, IoT connectivity enhances workflow coordination, material tracking, and quality control, leading to higher operational efficiency and lower production costs. Advanced Materials and Machining Techniques As new materials continue to emerge, CNC technology evolves to address the challenges they present. Advanced composites, high-entropy alloys (HEAs) , and next-generation polymers have unique machining requirements. High-entropy alloys are composed of multiple principal elements in near-equal proportions, offering exceptional strength, wear resistance, and thermal stability. These materials are increasingly used in aerospace and energy applications, where CNC machining must precisely control cutting forces and heat generation to maintain part integrity. CNC technology is also incorporating hybrid manufacturing techniques that combine additive manufacturing (3D printing) with traditional subtractive machining. These hybrid processes allow complex internal structures to be built additively and then finished with high-precision CNC cutting, making them ideal for lightweight aerospace components and customized medical implants. Human–Machine Collaboration and Augmented Reality Future CNC environments will emphasize human–machine collaboration, where operators work alongside intelligent machining systems rather than simply monitoring them. Augmented reality (AR) tools will support setup, training, and maintenance by overlaying digital instructions directly onto physical machinery. Technicians wearing AR headsets will be guided step-by-step through complex calibration or repair processes, reducing training time and lowering the risk of error. Furthermore, virtual simulation environments will allow engineers to preview machining operations before any material is cut. This not only helps validate designs but also ensures that tooling and fixturing are optimized for efficiency and safety. Conclusion Summary of Key Benefits CNC technology has transformed modern manufacturing by improving precision, efficiency, and flexibility. It enables complex machining, reduces errors, and accelerates production cycles. Impact on Modern Manufacturing With industrial CNC technology, advanced machines, and comprehensive services, manufacturers can achieve high-quality output, innovate rapidly, and maintain a competitive edge. As CNC technology continues to evolve, its influence on the manufacturing industry will only grow stronger. Every part produced from the same CNC program is virtually identical, minimizing variation and reducing scrap rates. This repeatability simplifies quality control processes, as fewer manual inspections are required once a process is stabilized. CNC systems also integrate easily with in-process measurement and inspection technologies, enabling real-time quality monitoring and early detection of deviations before defects occur. Material and Design Versatility CNC technology supports a wide range of materials, including metals, plastics, composites, and engineered alloys. From aluminum and stainless steel to advanced polymers and titanium, CNC machines can be optimized to handle different cutting characteristics and surface finish requirements. A common example is aluminum CNC machining , which is widely used due to aluminum’s excellent machinability and strength-to-weight ratio. In addition, CNC technology enables the machining of complex shapes, internal features, and intricate contours that would be extremely time-consuming or impractical with conventional methods. This design freedom allows engineers to innovate without being limited by manufacturing constraints. Scalability from Prototyping to Mass Production Another key advantage of CNC technology is its scalability. The same CNC setup can be used for rapid prototyping, small-batch production, and high-volume manufacturing with minimal modification. Design changes can be implemented quickly by updating the digital program rather than retooling entire production lines. This flexibility is particularly valuable for startups, R&D teams, and manufacturers operating in fast-moving markets where product iterations are frequent. Reduced Labor Dependency and Improved Safety By automating machining tasks, CNC technology reduces reliance on manual labor and lowers the risk of human error. Operators are less exposed to cutting tools and moving machine components, resulting in a safer working environment. Modern CNC systems also feature built-in safety controls, error detection, and machine monitoring functions that further protect both personnel and equipment while maintaining stable production. Cost Efficiency Over the Product Lifecycle While CNC machines require an initial investment, they offer long-term cost advantages. Reduced material waste, lower rework rates, shorter production times, and improved machine utilization all contribute to a lower cost per part over the product lifecycle. For manufacturers seeking consistent quality, predictable output, and efficient resource usage, CNC technology represents a cost-effective solution that supports sustainable growth. Applications of CNC Technology in Manufacturing CNC technology has a wide range of applications across industries due to its ability to deliver high precision, consistency, and production efficiency. From large-scale industrial manufacturing to rapid prototyping, CNC technology continues to expand as materials, software, and machine capabilities evolve. Applications in Metalworking CNC milling machines, lathes, and laser cutters handle metals like aluminum, steel, and titanium with unmatched precision. These machines reduce manual labor, minimize errors, and allow for complex shapes that meet rigorous industry standards. In metalworking industries where tolerance control and material consistency are critical, CNC technology enables reliable production of complex metal components at scale. Applications in Plastics and Woodworking Beyond metals, CNC routers can cut, engrave, and shape plastic components or wood panels with high accuracy. Routers are typically used for wood and plastic materials, while milling machines are better suited for metal machining due to their rigidity and cutting capabilities. Manufacturers can efficiently produce prototypes and mass-produced items, lowering production costs and turnaround times. Industrial Applications Industries such as automotive, aerospace, electronics, energy, and heavy machinery rely on CNC systems to produce structural components, housings, brackets, and precision parts. CNC machining ensures tight tolerances, repeatability, and high reliability for critical components. Prototyping and Small Batch Production Rapid prototyping and small-batch CNC production allow engineers to quickly transform digital designs into functional prototypes, enabling faster design validation, iterative testing, and reduced time-to-market. Innovative Uses in Various Industries Advanced applications such as multi-axis cutting, hybrid additive-subtractive manufacturing, and complex 3D contour machining expand possibilities in medical devices, architecture, and custom design. CNC Machine Technology Types of CNC Machines CNC machine technology includes milling machines, lathes, routers, plasma cutters, and laser engraving systems. Each type serves a specific function, from cutting and drilling to shaping and engraving, meeting diverse manufacturing needs. How CNC Machines Work CNC machines operate by translating digital designs into precise machining actions through integrated control systems. This enables highly accurate and repeatable production while minimizing material waste and optimizing workflow efficiency. Maintenance and Optimization Proper maintenance of CNC machines is essential for long-term performance. Regular calibration, tool replacement, and software updates optimize machine efficiency and prevent downtime. Skilled operators can further enhance productivity by choosing the right tooling and machining parameters. Industrial CNC Technology Automation in Large-Scale Production Industrial CNC technology enables full automation of production lines. Large-scale manufacturing can run continuously with minimal human supervision, improving throughput and reducing labor costs. Integration with Industrial Processes CNC technology integrates seamlessly with industrial processes such as assembly, quality inspection, and material handling. This integration allows for smarter factories, streamlined workflows, and higher overall efficiency. Case Studies Industries adopting industrial CNC technology have reported reduced production errors, faster turnaround times, and improved product consistency. For example, automotive suppliers use CNC machines to produce engine components with precise tolerances, enhancing vehicle performance and reliability. CNC Technology Services Design and Consulting Services CNC technology services extend beyond machining itself. Design and consulting services help manufacturers apply CNC technology effectively by optimizing material selection, machining strategies, and process planning before production begins. Manufacturing and Prototyping Services Service providers offer CNC machining for both prototypes and mass production. This allows businesses to outsource specialized tasks, reduce overhead, and maintain high-quality standards. Maintenance and Support Services Many CNC technology service providers also offer ongoing maintenance, troubleshooting, and training. This ensures clients can maintain efficient operations, extend machine lifespan, and minimize production delays. Future Trends in CNC Technology Beyond basic CNC operation and machine control, future CNC technology development is increasingly driven by intelligence, connectivity, and system-level integration. Future developments will not only improve precision and productivity but also fundamentally reshape how factories operate, how products are designed, and how manufacturers compete in global markets. Smart CNC and AI Integration The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with CNC systems is transforming machining from reactive automation into predictive and adaptive manufacturing. AI-powered algorithms can analyze historical machining data. They automatically optimize tool paths, reduce cycle times, and minimize tool wear. Machine learning models are increasingly used to detect subtle signs of tool degradation or misalignment before they cause defects. In aerospace and medical device manufacturing, where tolerances are extremely tight, AI-assisted CNC tool path optimization is already being adopted to ensure consistency and precision across complex geometries. Over time, smart CNC machines will be able to adjust cutting strategies in real time, self-correcting for material inconsistencies and dynamic load variations without human intervention. IoT and Connected Manufacturing The rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) enables CNC machines to become integral components of connected smart factories. Sensors embedded in CNC equipment collect real-time data on temperature, vibration, spindle load, and tool life. This data, streamed through secure networks, feeds into centralized manufacturing execution systems (MES) and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems to support real-time monitoring and informed decision-making. Connected CNC machines can automatically schedule maintenance based on actual usage patterns, reducing unplanned downtime. In facilities with multiple machines producing different parts, IoT connectivity enhances workflow coordination, material tracking, and quality control, leading to higher operational efficiency and lower production costs. Advanced Materials and Machining Techniques As new materials continue to emerge, CNC technology evolves to address the challenges they present. Advanced composites, high-entropy alloys (HEAs) , and next-generation polymers have unique machining requirements. High-entropy alloys are composed of multiple principal elements in near-equal proportions, offering exceptional strength, wear resistance, and thermal stability. These materials are increasingly used in aerospace and energy applications, where CNC machining must precisely control cutting forces and heat generation to maintain part integrity. CNC technology is also incorporating hybrid manufacturing techniques that combine additive manufacturing (3D printing) with traditional subtractive machining. These hybrid processes allow complex internal structures to be built additively and then finished with high-precision CNC cutting, making them ideal for lightweight aerospace components and customized medical implants. Human–Machine Collaboration and Augmented Reality Future CNC environments will emphasize human–machine collaboration, where operators work alongside intelligent machining systems rather than simply monitoring them. Augmented reality (AR) tools will support setup, training, and maintenance by overlaying digital instructions directly onto physical machinery. Technicians wearing AR headsets will be guided step-by-step through complex calibration or repair processes, reducing training time and lowering the risk of error. Furthermore, virtual simulation environments will allow engineers to preview machining operations before any material is cut. This not only helps validate designs but also ensures that tooling and fixturing are optimized for efficiency and safety. Conclusion Summary of Key Benefits CNC technology has transformed modern manufacturing by improving precision, efficiency, and flexibility. It enables complex machining, reduces errors, and accelerates production cycles. Impact on Modern Manufacturing With industrial CNC technology, advanced machines, and comprehensive services, manufacturers can achieve high-quality output, innovate rapidly, and maintain a competitive edge. As CNC technology continues to evolve, its influence on the manufacturing industry will only grow stronger. events.summary: 页面正文发生可定位的变化
events.before: Home Newsroom Notice on the Upcoming EU Tax Reform Effective July 2026 Notice on the Upcoming EU Tax Reform Effective July 2026 Press Release Jun 27, 2026 Table of Contents Policy Overview: Elimination of Duty Exemptions Different sets of rules will apply to B2C and B2B shipments Managing "Duty & Tax Disbursement Fees" from Carriers Consolidation Advice for B2C Shipments An official advisory has been issued for customers across the European Union regarding the upcoming EU Tax Reform . Effective July 1, 2026 , this major regulatory shift implemented by the European Union will impact import and customs procedures for low-value shipments entering EU member states. To ensure uninterrupted service and minimize clearance delays, all EU-based clients are urged to familiarize themselves with these new regulations. Policy Overview: Elimination of Duty Exemptions Starting July 1, 2026, the European Union will completely eliminate the customs duty exemption for low-value goods . Every single shipment bound for the EU, regardless of its value, must be formally declared and is subject to customs duties. Different sets of rules will apply to B2C and B2B shipments The EUCR introduces distinct compliance frameworks based on the nature of the recipient: 1. For B2C shipments : Goods value ≤ €150 : A flat-rate "temporary customs duty" of €3.00 per line item will be applied. For example, if a package contains 3 different product categories, the total temporary customs duty will be €9.00. Goods value > €150 : Standard tariff rates apply. Impact on IOSS : Under the current IOSS framework, JLCCNC can only collect and remit import VAT, but cannot manage the "temporary customs duty". Therefore, recipients will still need to pay the "temporary customs duty" upon importation if using non-DDP channels. 2. For B2B shipments : Regardless of the shipment value, all B2B packages must go through formal customs clearance and pay duties based on the actual HS code corresponding to the goods (standard applicable tariff rates), bypassing the €3.00 flat-rate rule. Managing "Duty & Tax Disbursement Fees" from Carriers When carriers like DHL, UPS, or FedEx pay customs duties and taxes upfront on behalf of the recipient, they charge a "duty & tax disbursement fee" to the party responsible for the tax. These fees vary significantly by country and carrier (such as tiered brackets or specific minimum charges per shipment). Consolidation Advice for B2C Shipments To optimize your shipping costs under the new EU regulations, we highly recommend consolidating your orders. For B2C customers, if you combine multiple items or orders into a single shipment to bring the total goods value above €150 , the shipment will become eligible for standard tariff rates instead of the €3.00 flat-rate temporary customs duty per line item. For many multi-item orders, utilizing standard tariffs through consolidation can be significantly more cost-effective. For more information regarding specific handling fees, tax calculations, and country-by-country Duty & Tax Disbursement Fee, please read our full EU Customs Reform (EUCR) July 2026 – Client FAQ . events.before: Home Newsroom JLC Technology Group Launches USDC Payments for Faster, Lower-Fee Checkout JLC Technology Group Launches USDC Payments for Faster, Lower-Fee Checkout Press Release Aug 27, 2026 Table of Contents Faster and Lower-Cost Payments with USDC USDC Payment Availability How to Pay with USDC USDC Payment FAQs Supporting a More Flexible Digital Manufacturing Experience About JLC Technology Group About JLCCNC We are thrilled to announce that JLC Technology Group now officially accepts stablecoin payments . US-based customers can now pay for JLCCNC, JLC3DP, JLCPCB, and JLCMC orders using USDC—enabling near-instant settlement, lower transaction fees, and 24/7 availability. Faster and Lower-Cost Payments with USDC Paying with stablecoins brings several tangible advantages directly to customers: Lower transaction costs – Customers only pay the blockchain network fee (Gas fee), which is typically a fraction of a dollar on networks like Solana or Polygon. There are no cross-border surcharges or hidden bank fees. No bank account or credit card required – Customers only need a crypto wallet, such as MetaMask or Coinbase Wallet. Fast and straightforward checkout – Customers can select stablecoin at checkout, connect their wallet, and confirm the transaction in just a few clicks, without entering lengthy card details or bank information. In short, USDC payments provide lower fees, instant processing, and a smoother checkout experience. USDC Payment Availability The current stablecoin payment setup includes the following conditions: Item Current Rule Supported business JLCPCB, JLC3DP, JLCCNC, and JLCMC Supported region United States only Supported stablecoin USDC only Supported networks Tempo, Ethereum, Solana, Polygon, Base Maximum per transaction Up to 10,000 USD Refund options Original wallet or JLC balance These rules reflect JLC's current stablecoin payment setup. Customers outside the United States will not see the USDC payment option at this stage. Any future expansion of supported regions will be announced separately. This launch supports USDC only . Other stablecoins, including USDP and USDG, are not currently supported. How to Pay with USDC Paying with stablecoins is simple and requires four steps. Step 1: Select Payment Method at Checkout On the JLC order confirmation page, select "Crypto (USDC)" . Step 2: Connect Your Crypto Wallet Customers will be redirected to a secure payment page, where they can connect using MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet , or any WalletConnect-compatible wallet. Step 3: Confirm and Sign the Transaction The payment page displays the amount due, denominated in USDC and pegged 1:1 to USD. Customers can confirm and sign the transaction in their wallet. Step 4: Payment Complete Once the transaction is confirmed on-chain, the order status will update automatically. Funds are settled in USD to JLC's account — JLC does not hold or manage any cryptocurrency. USDC Payment FAQs Q1: Which stablecoins are currently supported? USDC only. Other stablecoins, including USDT, USDP, and USDG, are not currently supported. Q2: Are there fees for stablecoin payments? Customers are responsible for the Gas fees (network transaction fees) of the chosen blockchain network. Fees vary by network — Solana, Polygon, and Base offer extremely low fees, often just a few cents. JLC Technology Group does not charge any additional fees for stablecoin payments. Q3: Is there a transaction limit? The per-transaction limit is 10,000 USD. Orders exceeding this amount are not eligible for stablecoin payment and require an alternative payment method. Q4: Are refunds supported? Yes. Refunds are processed back to the customer's original wallet or to the customer's JLC balance, subject to customer setup. Q5: Which regions are supported? Currently, stablecoin payments are available only for customers in the United States. Other countries are not supported at this time. Q6: How long does a stablecoin payment take to confirm? Confirmation time varies by network. Ethereum typically takes 3–15 minutes, while Solana, Polygon, and Base usually confirm within 5–30 seconds. During network congestion, times may be longer. Customers are recommended to use faster networks like Solana or Polygon for the quickest experience. Supporting a More Flexible Digital Manufacturing Experience The launch of USDC payments provides US-based customers with another way to complete orders across JLC Technology Group's digital manufacturing ecosystem. By supporting stablecoin payments, JLCCNC and other JLC platforms provide customers with a payment option designed around faster processing, lower transaction costs, and 24/7 availability. About JLC Technology Group Founded in 2006, JLC Technology Group provides integrated electronics and mechanical manufacturing services to more than 9.5 million customers across over 180 countries and regions. Its ecosystem includes EasyEDA for PCB design, JLCPCB for PCB fabrication and assembly, JLC3DP for additive manufacturing, JLCCNC for CNC machining and sheet metal fabrication, and JLCMC for mechanical components—enabling customers to move from prototype to production through a full-stack digital manufacturing platform. About JLCCNC JLCCNC is an online manufacturing platform providing professional CNC machining and sheet metal fabrication services for engineers, product developers, businesses, and makers worldwide. With a range of manufacturing capabilities and materials, JLCCNC helps customers accelerate prototyping and production with quality, speed, and affordability. As part of JLC Technology Group , JLCCNC provides customers with access to the group's integrated digital manufacturing ecosystem, including electronics manufacturing, 3D printing, and mechanical components. USDC Payment Availability The current stablecoin payment setup includes the following conditions: Item Current Rule Supported business JLCPCB, JLC3DP, JLCCNC, and JLCMC Supported region United States only Supported stablecoin USDC only Supported networks Tempo, Ethereum, Solana, Polygon, Base Maximum per transaction Up to 10,000 USD Refund options Original wallet or JLC balance These rules reflect JLC's current stablecoin payment setup. Customers outside the United States will not see the USDC payment option at this stage. Any future expansion of supported regions will be announced separately. This launch supports USDC only . Other stablecoins, including USDP and USDG, are not currently supported. How to Pay with USDC Paying with stablecoins is simple and requires four steps. Step 1: Select Payment Method at Checkout On the JLC order confirmation page, select "Crypto (USDC)" . Step 2: Connect Your Crypto Wallet Customers will be redirected to a secure payment page, where they can connect using MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet , or any WalletConnect-compatible wallet. Step 3: Confirm and Sign the Transaction The payment page displays the amount due, denominated in USDC and pegged 1:1 to USD. Customers can confirm and sign the transaction in their wallet. Step 4: Payment Complete Once the transaction is confirmed on-chain, the order status will update automatically. Funds are settled in USD to JLC's account — JLC does not hold or manage any cryptocurrency. USDC Payment FAQs Q1: Which stablecoins are currently supported? USDC only. Other stablecoins, including USDT, USDP, and USDG, are not currently supported. Q2: Are there fees for stablecoin payments? Customers are responsible for the Gas fees (network transaction fees) of the chosen blockchain network. Fees vary by network — Solana, Polygon, and Base offer extremely low fees, often just a few cents. JLC Technology Group does not charge any additional fees for stablecoin payments. Q3: Is there a transaction limit? The per-transaction limit is 10,000 USD. Orders exceeding this amount are not eligible for stablecoin payment and require an alternative payment method. Q4: Are refunds supported? Yes. Refunds are processed back to the customer's original wallet or to the customer's JLC balance, subject to customer setup. Q5: Which regions are supported? Currently, stablecoin payments are available only for customers in the United States. Other countries are not supported at this time. Q6: How long does a stablecoin payment take to confirm? Confirmation time varies by network. Ethereum typically takes 3–15 minutes, while Solana, Polygon, and Base usually confirm within 5–30 seconds. During network congestion, times may be longer. Customers are recommended to use faster networks like Solana or Polygon for the quickest experience. Supporting a More Flexible Digital Manufacturing Experience The launch of USDC payments provides US-based customers with another way to complete orders across JLC Technology Group's digital manufacturing ecosystem. By supporting stablecoin payments, JLCCNC and other JLC platforms provide customers with a payment option designed around faster processing, lower transaction costs, and 24/7 availability. About JLC Technology Group Founded in 2006, JLC Technology Group provides integrated electronics and mechanical manufacturing services to more than 9.5 million customers across over 180 countries and regions. Its ecosystem includes EasyEDA for PCB design, JLCPCB for PCB fabrication and assembly, JLC3DP for additive manufacturing, JLCCNC for CNC machining and sheet metal fabrication, and JLCMC for mechanical components—enabling customers to move from prototype to production through a full-stack digital manufacturing platform. About JLCCNC JLCCNC is an online manufacturing platform providing professional CNC machining and sheet metal fabrication services for engineers, product developers, businesses, and makers worldwide. With a range of manufacturing capabilities and materials, JLCCNC helps customers accelerate prototyping and production with quality, speed, and affordability. As part of JLC Technology Group , JLCCNC provides customers with access to the group's integrated digital manufacturing ecosystem, including electronics manufacturing, 3D printing, and mechanical components. events.before: Home Newsroom JLC Digital Manufacturing Achieves PCI DSS v4.0.1 Level 1 Certification JLC Digital Manufacturing Achieves PCI DSS v4.0.1 Level 1 Certification Press Release Jul 24, 2026 Table of Contents Strengthening Payment Security for Global Customers Secure Payment Infrastructure Supporting Secure Digital Manufacturing About JLC Digital Manufacturing JLC Digital Manufacturing has achieved Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) v4.0.1 Level 1 certification , the highest level of PCI DSS compliance. The certification covers the company's major overseas business platforms, including JLCCNC, JLCPCB, JLC3DP, and JLCMC , reinforcing payment security and data protection for customers worldwide. The certification was independently assessed by atsec information security , a Qualified Security Assessor (QSA). This achievement builds upon JLC Digital Manufacturing's previously obtained ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information Security Management System and ISO/IEC 27701:2019 Privacy Information Management System certifications, further strengthening the company's information security governance framework and its commitment to secure cross-border digital services. Strengthening Payment Security for Global Customers PCI DSS is the internationally recognized security standard established by major international payment card brands, including Visa and MasterCard, to protect payment card information. Version 4.0.1 establishes comprehensive security requirements covering areas such as network protection, encryption, access control, vulnerability management, security monitoring, and governance. By achieving PCI DSS v4.0.1 Level 1 certification, JLC Digital Manufacturing demonstrates that its payment security controls have been independently assessed against internationally recognized industry standards. For customers, this certification provides additional confidence that payment information is protected according to globally accepted security requirements throughout the online transaction process. Secure Payment Infrastructure JLC Digital Manufacturing protects online payments through industry-standard encryption, secure tokenization technologies, and trusted payment service providers, including Stripe and PayPal. The company's payment architecture is designed to protect cardholder information during transmission while reducing the handling of sensitive payment data within its own systems. In accordance with PCI DSS requirements, JLC Digital Manufacturing does not store unencrypted cardholder data, helping minimize potential security risks. These security measures support the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of payment information for customers conducting business through the company's global digital platforms. Supporting Secure Digital Manufacturing As AI technologies and intelligent manufacturing continue to accelerate the evolution of the electronics industry, cybersecurity and payment security have become increasingly important across global supply chains. For JLC Digital Manufacturing, protecting customer information and enabling secure online transactions are fundamental to delivering reliable digital manufacturing services. With internationally recognized certifications including ISO/IEC 27001 , ISO/IEC 27701 , and PCI DSS v4.0.1 Level 1 , JLC Digital Manufacturing will continue enhancing its security capabilities while providing trusted services for engineers, innovators, and businesses worldwide. About JLC Digital Manufacturing Founded in 2006, JLC Digital Manufacturing provides integrated electronics and mechanical manufacturing services to more than 9.5 million customers across over 180 countries and regions . Its ecosystem includes JLCCNC for CNC machining and sheet metal fabrication, EasyEDA for PCB design, JLCPCB for PCB fabrication, component sourcing, and PCB assembly, JLC3DP for additive manufacturing, and JLCMC for mechanical components, enabling customers to move from prototype to production through a full-stack digital manufacturing platform. For JLCCNC customers, this certification provides additional assurance that online payment information is protected according to internationally recognized security standards. events.before: Home Newsroom JLCCNC Participates in Hannover Messe 2025 JLCCNC Participates in Hannover Messe 2025 Press Release Mar 10, 2025 JLCCNC will exhibit at Hannover Messe from 31 March to 4 April 2025 at Hannover Messe in Germany. With the theme of ‘Energising A Sustainable Industry’, JLC Global will be showcasing its full range of technologies in 3D printing, CNC machining, Mechanical Components, PCB, PCBA and PCB design software development in Hall 17, Booth B12, demonstrating its expertise in smart manufacturing and digital transformation. It demonstrates its leading strength in the field of intelligent manufacturing and digital transformation. Exhibition Information · Event Theme : Hannover Messe 2025 - "Energizing A Sustainable Industry" · Dates : March 31 to April 4, 2025 · Location : Hannover Exhibition Center, 30521 Hannover, Germany · JLCCNC Booth : Hall 17, Stand B12 (together with JLCPCB) · Exhibits : 3D Printing, CNC Machining, Mechanical Components , PCB, PCBA, PCB Design Software Development 1. Exhibition Background As one of the world's largest and most influential industrial events, Hannover Messe has always been the wind vane for global industrial automation, digital manufacturing and sustainable industrial development. With the theme of ‘Energising A Sustainable Industry’, this year's fair focuses on green energy, intelligent manufacturing and sustainable development, and attracts many global leading enterprises and experts to gather and discuss the new trends of future industry. 2. About JLC Global JLC Global is a comprehensive technology company dedicated to promoting industrial intelligence and digital transformation. The company focuses on the R&D and production of 3D printing, CNC machining, automated production, and the whole industry chain of electronic manufacturing such as PCB and PCBA. Relying on strong technological strength and innovative R&D capabilities, JLC Global continues to provide efficient and accurate manufacturing solutions for global customers and leads the industry with continuous technological innovation. In recent years, JLC Global has made remarkable achievements in the field of intelligent manufacturing and green production, and has successfully implemented a number of major projects to create a sustainable and efficient production system for its customers. 3. Exhibition Highlights and Product/Technology Details In this Hannover Messe, JLC Global will comprehensively display the core technologies and innovative products of its entire business line, specifically including: CNC Machining : The company will display advanced CNC machining systems to ensure efficient and accurate parts machining capability. 3D Printing : Showcasing high-precision, rapid prototyping 3D printing technology to meet diversified industrial manufacturing needs. Mechanical Components : JLC Mechatronic Components Marketplace integrates various mechatronic parts, aiming to provide a one-stop service for factory automation. PCB & PCBA : Showcasing the whole industry chain services from PCB design, manufacturing to assembly, helping the rapid iteration of electronic products. PCB Design Software Development : Introducing self-developed PCB design software to enhance design efficiency and product innovation. At the exhibition site, visitors will have the opportunity to fully understand JLC Global's innovations in process, technology and products, and deeply experience the company's all-round solutions in the field of intelligent manufacturing through interactive experience. 4. More Information For more exhibition activities and the latest news of JLCCNC, please visit our official website and follow our official social media platforms. We will be arranging on-site experts to answer questions and provide technical demonstrations, and we sincerely invite all professionals to come and exchange views, and witness the future changes of industrial technology together. If you have CNC machining needs, click to get a free quote for our cnc machining services. The Lunar New Year holiday will span from January 23rd to February 4th . All CNC Machining materials will continue production during the LNY holiday, except for Steel 45#, SUS304. Spray Painting service is unavailable . Note: The build time might be 2-3 days longer than usual during the LNY holiday. During the Lunar New Year holiday, 3D printing and CNC machining orders cannot be combined for shipping, nor can they be combined with PCB/Stencil orders. This will resume on February 5th. Below is the production and shipping schedule. Please kindly schedule the order placement time properly to guarantee the timely completion of your projects. Prior to this, PCBWay successfully held six design contests. In each contest, we saw many eye-catching projects shared by outstanding and creative electronic engineers and enthusiasts. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest will continue the previous purpose, which is to encourage more and more people to explore the charm of electronic design and participate in it. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . In this contest, in addition to the two themes of Electronic Project and Mechanical Project that have appeared before, we also introduced STM32 Project, hoping to give designers more room to perform. The contest will start on September 2nd, 2024, and project submissions will be accepted until January 19th, 2025. After this, the judging phase will begin, and the final winners will be announced on the PCBWay Blog on March 10th, 2025. Two ways to participate in the contest: Go to the contest page, find the Participate Now button and click it. In this case, the submitted project will automatically be entered into the competition; participants only need to select the theme of entry. Please note that if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. After filling in all the project information, simply click "Submit" at the bottom of the page. Go to the SharedProject Community ( https://www.pcbway.com/project/shareproject/ ) and click Create a project. Select the theme you are going to participate in. Similarly, if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. Hint: Sharing complete project files, including Gerber, BOM, Centroid file, schematics, 3D files, and so on will increase the chances of receiving a higher score. Awards and corresponding prizes: The First Prize : 1 winner, $1500 Cash + $200 Coupon + A Palm-sized Robot Dog*1 The Second Prize : 2 winners, $1000 Cash + $100 Coupon + Raspberry Pi 5 4GB *1 The Third Prize : 3 winners, $500 Cash + $50 Coupon + OpenMV4 H7 R2 Cam Smart Camera *1 Popular Design Prize : 10 winners, $100 Cash + $20 Coupon + $10 3D Printing Coupon + Multimeter ZTY890DPro *1 Participation Prize : Raspberry Pi Pico * 1 STM32 Great Project Prize : Six-Claw Multifunctional Aluminum Alloy Soldering Table *1 For more detailed information about the contest, please refer to: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . If there are any questions or suggestions, feel free to leave a comment below.We wish you the best of luck and look forward to your innovative designs! Verify Now Blog > Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay by: PCBWay May 30,2025 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News PCBWay recognizes the significant role it plays within the supply chain and broader society, along with the potential impact of its operations. To this end, we have established and strictly enforce the following principles, which not only govern our own conduct but also set clear expectations for our partners. Our goal is to ensure full legal and regulatory compliance, promote long-term sustainability, and generate a positive impact on society. Human Rights and Labor Protection No employment of individuals below the legal working age; all forms of forced or bonded labor are strictly prohibited. Discrimination and harassment in the workplace are not tolerated; an inclusive work environment for persons with disabilities is encouraged. Employees must be provided with fair compensation and reasonable rest periods, and their rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining must be respected. Business Ethics and Compliance Offering, promising, soliciting, or accepting any form of bribery is strictly prohibited; effective conflict of interest management and whistleblowing mechanisms must be in place. All financial and business records must accurately, completely, and truthfully reflect the underlying transactions. Full compliance with international sanctions, export controls, and other applicable laws and regulations is required. Supply Chain Responsibility and Sustainable Procurement PCBWay and its partners are required to extend the principles outlined in this document to all levels of entities within the supply chain. Priority should be given to selecting partners that are legally compliant, socially responsible, and committed to sustainable development. Identify social, labor, and environmental risks related to operations, and develop corresponding control and mitigation measures. Encourage partners to prioritize local sourcing to support regional economic development and job creation. Environmental Protection and Workplace Safety Actively implement environmental protection measures and continuously promote energy conservation and emission reduction; Ensure that all waste and hazardous materials are disposed of in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. The procurement or use of prohibited materials is not allowed. Provide employees with a safe working environment and health support mechanisms to prevent occupational injuries and health risks. PCBWay has fully adopted the DHL GoGreen transportation service in 2025 to reduce carbon emissions in the supply chain and promote the development of a green supply chain, with an initial target of reducing emissions by 30%. Information Protection and Transparent Governance Establish a comprehensive security system to strictly protect the confidentiality of customer data, drawings, and other business information. Comply with relevant laws and regulations to safeguard the personal data of customers and employees. Ensure that financial records are true, accurate, and complete, and prohibit any illegal activities. PCBWay will ensure the implementation of the above principles in actual cooperation and reserves the right to take action against any violations.
